item.research_question: How does high configurational entropy affect the correlation between calorimetric and dynamical glass transitions, and what is the underlying mechanism for the observed decoupling in high-entropy metallic glasses?
item.material_system: La55Ni20Al25, Ce55Ni20Al25, La27.5Ce27.5Ni20Al25 (LaCe-HEMG); Pd42.5Cu30Ni7.5P20, Pt57.5Cu14.7Ni5.3P22.5, Pd20Pt20Cu20Ni20P20 (PdPt-HEMG); Zr50Cu20Ni20Al10, Ti50Cu20Ni20Al10, Ti25Zr25Cu20Ni20Al10 (TiZr-HEMG)
item.processing_route: Arc-melting of raw metals (purity >99.9 mass %) in Ar atmosphere with Ti getter; melt-spinning onto a single Cu wheel at 3000 r.p.m. using Ar gas overpressure to produce glassy ribbons (thickness ~50 μm); ion milling (3 kV, then 0.5 kV with liquid nitrogen cooling) for TEM specimens
item.test_conditions: DSC heating rates of 0.33 K s−1 and 25–600 K s−1; DMA at 1 Hz with heating rate 0.05 K s−1 and frequencies 0.5–16 Hz; TMA heating rate 0.33 K s−1 with 0.1 N load; XRD after heating to Tx; TEM at 200 kV
key_findings: LaCe-HEMG exhibits the highest α-relaxation temperature (Tα) despite having an intermediate calorimetric Tg, demonstrating decoupling between thermal and dynamic transitions.
The mixing entropy (ΔSmix) values are 1.38 R, 1.67 R, and 1.57 R for LaCe-HEMG, PdPt-HEMG, and TiZr-HEMG, respectively, all exceeding the 1.36 R threshold for high entropy.
LaCe-HEMG shows the lowest fragility (m = 35) compared to La55Ni20Al25 (m = 42) and Ce55Ni20Al25 (m = 39), indicating strong glass behavior.
The activation energy for α-relaxation (Eα) in LaCe-HEMG is 267.6 kJ mol−1, higher than Ce55Ni20Al25 (229.8 kJ mol−1) and La55Ni20Al25 (249.6 kJ mol−1).
STEM analysis reveals LaCe-HEMG has the smallest nanoscale domain size (1.851 ± 0.206 nm) compared to La55Ni20Al25 (2.491 ± 0.297 nm) and Ce55Ni20Al25 (2.380 ± 0.248 nm).
LaCe-HEMG exhibits high resistance to crystallization with few precipitates of ~8 ± 1.7 nm nanocrystals, whereas traditional MGs show widespread crystalline grains around 100 nm.
The activation energy for β-relaxation (Eβ) in LaCe-HEMG is 88.8 kJ mol−1, intermediate between Ce55Ni20Al25 (85.8 kJ mol−1) and La55Ni20Al25 (93.9 kJ mol−1).
item.mechanism: The authors propose that high mixing entropy suppresses dynamic and spatial heterogeneities, leading to smaller, more homogeneous nanoscale domains (~2 nm) analogous to shear transformation zones (STZs). This homogeneity, combined with sluggish diffusion, inhibits the long-range cooperative atomic rearrangement required for α-relaxation and crystallization, thereby elevating the activation energy and Tα without significantly altering the calorimetric Tg, which is governed by local thermal diffusion.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that the HEA 'core effect' (sluggish diffusion on spatial heterogeneity) will provide freedom to solve fundamental issues such as the glass transition, relaxations, and aging behaviors of metallic glasses.
quotes: HEMGs with moderate calorimetric Tg represent the highest Tα and the maximum activation energy of α-relaxation.
LaCe-HEMG, with a modest thermodynamic devitrification behavior, exhibits the uppermost dynamic glass-transition process.
